title: Organization, legal, business-day, and operations settings
summary: Implement tenant settings for organization/legal profile, locale/timezone, tax/document profile, business day, service windows, cutoffs, holidays, operational minimums, and effective policy revisions.
steps: Define each setting's owner, scope, effective time, validation, required authority, audit event, and historic snapshot consequence.
Validate legal/document requirements before issue/export while allowing incomplete setup as an explicit activation state.
Apply future operational changes to future work without rewriting issued document, price, route, or source history.

Model the three independent confirmation gates and their combined effective-policy copy; a durable-write failure retains the previous effective snapshot and returns focus to the labelled failed setting.

positive: A permitted effective-dated cutoff change affects only future eligible operational projections.

A permitted operator can change one confirmation policy field without resetting the other remembered choices, and the persisted effective policy explains whether a customer message may show current prices.
negative: An incomplete profile, client timezone, or unsaved setting cannot silently produce a legally complete document or mutate historic work.
A preview, local toggle, hidden albarán value or failed durable write cannot send a message, invent a price, erase another choice, or replace the prior effective policy.

doneConditions: Every organization/business/operations control has command, state, exact copy, authority, audit, and effective-date tests.
JNY-C03–JNY-C08 and JNY-P03 have authorized command, revision, remembered-choice, save-failure, accessible-name, focus-return and customer-copy tests.
requiredEvidence: Settings contract suite, incomplete-profile issue denial, and effective-date projection trace.
Confirmation-policy command trace covering all three gate combinations, previous-value retention on write failure, and no-send preview denial.

title: Team, access, security, and personal-preference settings
summary: Build all team invite/role/suspend/remove/ownership-transfer/session-revoke controls and separate tenant policy from individual locale, notification, accessibility, default-view, and saved-filter preferences.
steps: Route membership and sensitive access acts through strong authority and immediate revocation semantics.
Store user preferences in personal scope and tenant settings in tenant scope, each with independent revision and audit.
Expose invite, pending, active, suspended, removed, ownership-transfer, error, and recovery states with exact visible/accessibility copy.
Keep each salesperson line/account assignment personal and tenant-scoped during first-time setup; a later line does not inherit another line’s owner or customer scope.
Model a manager-authorised cross-cover grant as a bounded actor/line/account/time scope with independent audit, expiry and revocation; it never transfers ownership or widens tenant access.

positive: A permitted owner suspension immediately blocks the affected member's new commands and subscriptions.
A permitted owner can assign distinct named salesperson ownership to independently configured lines.
A permitted manager can grant bounded cross-cover while the covering salesperson sees only the named temporary scope.
negative: A user preference, invite, stale session, or role editor cannot alter tenant policy or self-grant an unavailable capability.
A team preference, stale session or line chip cannot grant another salesperson’s accounts or provider authority.
An owner chip, default filter, stale session or cross-cover proposal cannot self-widen account, output or messaging authority.

doneConditions: Every team/security/preference control has role, conflict, revoke, invite, accessibility, and audit coverage.
requiredEvidence: Role transition tests, session-revocation trace, and preference-scope audit.
Two-line owner assignment/revoke and setup-resume scope audit.
Cross-cover grant/expiry/revoke/cross-tenant denial and salesperson-scope audit.

title: Automation, geography, fulfilment, and app-policy settings
summary: Configure automation grants, budgets, notification escalation, zones, routes, trucks, inventory policy, delivery evidence policy, and per-user application behavior as separate revisioned settings domains.
steps: Define every automation/grant threshold, route, stock exception, notification, and preference control with scope and activation review.
Require policy simulation/test lineage before enabling an automation or fulfilment policy that can affect live work.
Make disable, pause, revoke, and policy conflict visible without deleting history or already accepted job evidence.
Define the recurring-request review and ERP-line policy as independent revisioned settings: no automatic SKU admission, base-item-note by default, and mapped variation only after approved mapping.

positive: A reviewed grant enables only its tenant-scoped allowed action and produces a policy/audit trail.
A tenant can keep recurring requests as notes or explicitly permit reviewed mapped-variation handling while the customer-visible draft distinguishes the selected policy.
negative: A setting toggle, map choice, or app preference cannot bypass required review, change past records, or silently send externally.
Repeated source wording, a setting preview or missing destination mapping cannot create a SKU, create an ERP item, silently map a variation, or claim a live ERP sync.

doneConditions: All automation/geography/operations/app setting controls have state, permission, simulation, and revocation tests.
JNY-P01–JNY-P02 have policy revision, approval-gate, customer-visible distinction, missing-mapping and no-auto-SKU tests.
requiredEvidence: Policy simulation report, grant audit, and disabled-automation rejection test.
Product-request policy audit showing no automatic SKU/ERP creation and a rejected mapped-variation request without approved mapping.

title: Plan, subscription billing, invoices, and restricted-state controls
summary: Implement Rocoto subscription plan, seat/usage state, billing contact, payment-method portal request, invoices, cancellation/reactivation, and policy-defined restricted access independently from customer receivables.
steps: Model subscription status, plan, seats, usage, billing contact, invoices, provider event, and policy outcome with tenant ownership.
Use provider webhook/portal receipts as separate facts from requested changes and show retry/unknown state.
Define restriction behavior that preserves policy-allowed read/export/recovery rights while blocking new high-risk acts.

positive: An authorized billing event updates tenant subscription state only after verified provider evidence.
negative: A customer payment, frontend plan label, stale usage meter, or unverified callback cannot change subscription authority.

doneConditions: Plan, invoice, billing-contact, provider-event, restriction, cancellation, and reactivation tests pass.
requiredEvidence: Billing event fixture, restricted-state command denial, and provider reconciliation audit.

title: Data administration, privacy requests, retention, and legal hold
summary: Operate tenant data inventory, retention, export-all, access report, rectification, redaction/delete request, legal hold, recovery window, and support approval as auditable policy-controlled jobs.
steps: Classify each request by authority, tenant, subject, scope, retention/legal-hold constraints, and reversible/irreversible effect.
Execute exports, redactions, and deletion requests as job records with review, progress, receipt, and recovery window.
Protect issued documents and retained evidence under declared legal/retention policy while minimizing sheet/export fields.

positive: An approved tenant data export has a bounded artifact, audit, expiry, and download authorization record.
negative: A request, support user, client filter, or expired link cannot cross tenant scope, bypass legal hold, or erase protected history.

doneConditions: Data lifecycle, export, retention, hold, redaction, access report, and support-approval tests pass.
requiredEvidence: Privacy-job audit, legal-hold denial test, and bounded export artifact manifest.

title: Administration navigation, setting inventory, and controlled founder operations
summary: Make all administration sections and their control inventories reachable, scope-correct, searchable, and auditable, including approved tenant provisioning and operational overview for authorized operators.
steps: Publish a machine-readable settings/control inventory with section, authority, command, state, copy, and test owner.
Provision tenant, owner, invite/link, and intake authorization through controlled founder/operator commands with audit and no silent fixture creation.
Present operator overview as scoped operational projections, not access to raw tenants or private source content.

Expose the Product Sheet confirmation door and Operations Customer confirmations row/deep route as one shared in-place settings modal, with named close/Done behavior, focus return, Back/Forward selected-preview restoration and no implied send.

positive: An authorized operator can provision one tenant and retrieve its explicit activation/intake state without reading unrelated tenant data.
An authorized user can open the scoped customer-confirmations settings surface from the product door and return to the invoking context without changing a message or business record.
negative: Navigation, a founder-facing view, or an unscoped provisioning request cannot expose credentials, private source contents, or cross-tenant operations.
A route, sheet close, Done action or stale client navigation state cannot grant policy authority, persist unsaved work, send a preview, or expose another tenant.

doneConditions: Every settings section/control is mapped; provisioning, tenant scope, link revoke, and operator read tests pass.
JNY-C01–JNY-C02 and JNY-P04 have Product/Operations entry, modal history restore, role, focus-return, responsive surface and no-second-command tests.
requiredEvidence: Settings inventory report, provisioning audit, and cross-tenant operator denial test.
Settings inventory report plus keyboard/focus/history trace for the Product door, Operations row/deep route and Done close behavior.

title: Asynchronous job orchestration, retries, and dead letters
summary: Provide the tenant-safe durable job backbone for imports, exports, rendering, sync, intelligence, scans, image work, data lifecycle, retries, cancellation, reconciliation, and manual recovery.
steps: Persist job intent, tenant, actor, source/object revisions, idempotency, priority, state, attempts, and result/receipt references.
Use bounded retry/backoff/cancel/dead-letter behavior and check staleness/authority before every effect.
Offer authorized replay/repair that creates a new audit attempt and never overwrites the original outcome.

positive: A failed job exposes a durable failure/retry state and can resume safely with the same or explicitly new idempotency contract.
negative: A worker crash, duplicate delivery, stale revision, or cancelled job cannot cause unbounded retries, duplicate effects, or fabricated completion.

doneConditions: Job idempotency, retry, cancel, dead-letter, tenant isolation, stale work, and manual replay tests pass.
requiredEvidence: Job state trace, dead-letter report, and controlled replay audit.

title: Operational observability, alerts, and incident mode
summary: Instrument health, dependency status, queue/projection/cursor lag, provider state, auth anomalies, data job failures, backup status, and incident acknowledgement without exposing sensitive payloads.
steps: Define service and business integrity signals with threshold, freshness, tenant impact, owner, and recovery runbook.
Record alert acknowledgement, escalation, incident state, and remediation commands separately from raw source/business payloads.
Show operator health states as known, stale, degraded, failed, or unknown with timestamp/evidence.

positive: A projection lag or repeated receipt failure triggers a traceable alert with a documented investigation path.
negative: A green-looking dashboard, missing metric, or generic provider icon cannot mask unknown/stale health or leak sensitive content.

doneConditions: Metrics, alert, incident, authorization, and redaction tests plus an alert drill are completed.
requiredEvidence: Alert drill record, health dashboard snapshot, and incident audit trace.

title: Backup, restore, projection rebuild, and disaster recovery
summary: Operate encrypted, policy-compliant backups and isolated restore/replay exercises that prove recovery point/time objectives, projection parity, document integrity, access control, and cutover readiness.
steps: Encrypt and classify backups, record backup/restore exercise metadata, and restrict access with audit.
Restore into an isolated environment and rebuild projections from events/outbox with count/hash/sequence/snapshot parity checks.
Document recovery decision, RPO/RTO measurement, residual gap, compensating plan, and operator ownership.

positive: A controlled restore proves tenant scope, event sequence, projection parity, and issued document snapshot integrity.
negative: A backup success signal, raw snapshot, or recovery command cannot expose data, replace production silently, or skip parity validation.

doneConditions: Restore/rebuild exercise reaches the stated recovery objectives and records all parity checks.
requiredEvidence: Backup manifest, isolated restore report, and projection/document parity result.

title: Performance, availability, and recovery-user experience
summary: Measure and enforce interactive command/read budgets, job progress, large-data behavior, slow/degraded dependency behavior, mobile rendering, and recoverable user-state copy.
steps: Set and measure explicit query/command budgets, job performance, large history/catalogue limits, and degraded-dependency behavior.
Use bounded pagination/virtualization/deferred media and never block an interactive command transaction on external work.
Keep valid drafts and name exact object/revision/action in pending, failed, conflict, or unknown recovery states.

positive: A degraded external dependency preserves interactive local validation and reports its exact unavailable/pending state.
negative: A time-out, large list, slow network, or provider delay cannot block indefinitely, suppress errors, or show a cheerful success.

doneConditions: Cold/warm, slow network, large catalogue/history, mobile, degraded provider, and recovery-copy tests meet published budgets.
requiredEvidence: Performance report, budget dashboard, and degraded-dependency interaction trace.

title: Security, privacy, media safety, and least-privilege enforcement
summary: Implement defense-in-depth tenant policy, server authorization, secure session/request controls, encrypted storage, signed scoped files, malware scanning, webhook verification, egress controls, and secret-safe operations.
steps: Enforce tenant/role policy in database and server layers, and minimize projections/exports by action.
Use secure sessions, CSRF/XSS/CSP/rate/size/type controls, opaque secret references, signed files, and scan/quarantine gates.
Audit high-risk attempts, access/read acts, support grants, egress, and administrative actions with redacted summaries.

positive: A permitted scoped file download is auditable, time-bounded, and inaccessible after expiry/revocation.
negative: A client filter, unverified webhook, raw file, support request, or UI flag cannot bypass tenant scope, scanner, policy, or secret boundary.

doneConditions: Threat, authz, file, webhook, egress, rate, scanning, privacy, and support-access tests are green.
requiredEvidence: Security test report, dependency/secret review, and abuse-path denial evidence.

title: Full control/state accessibility and copy quality assurance
summary: Verify every mapped control, opened menu/form, individual field, validation, pending/error/provider state, accessible name, keyboard path, screen-reader announcement, and locale behavior against canonical anatomy/copy tables.
steps: Compare the control/copy inventory with implemented selectors/routes and report unmapped or ambiguous actions.
Test focus, labels, fields, errors, conflict, permission, pending, unavailable, and recovery messages on desktop/narrow layouts.
Verify translations preserve tenant-entered names, identifiers, values, links, and source evidence while missing strings remain explicit.
Read E188 list-card, unvalued-order, quantity/unit, Filters and phone keyboard/thumb states at the named viewports; verify concise operator copy and no founder/architecture narration in working UI.

positive: Each control state has a named action, scope, accessible name, expected copy, and evidence route.
negative: A missing label, translated business value, inaccessible chart, hidden error, or unmapped interactive action cannot pass release evidence.
Visible order money, full-width list hover, parallel filter controls, clipped terminal units, keyboard-obscured actions or founder/architecture narration cannot pass E188 evidence.

doneConditions: Control/copy completeness, automated accessibility, keyboard/screen-reader, narrow-layout, and locale integrity tests pass.
E188 current/hover/focus, long-line, draft-filter and keyboard/dock screenshot review passes at the named desktop and phone viewports.
requiredEvidence: Control coverage report, accessibility audit, copy diff, and locale identity-preservation test.
E188 visual matrix with list, line, filter and phone-keyboard/dock evidence; kit proof remains distinct from runtime execution.

title: Tenant provisioning, intake, and empty-state onboarding
summary: Guide a newly provisioned tenant through owner verification, organization setup, catalogue/source intake, review, and honest empty states with no production demo data or fake operational readiness.
steps: Model provisioned, organization-ready, intake, catalogue-ready, operations-ready, tested, activated, restricted, and closed states from facts.
Guide owner through authorized source upload/review in the shared bounded task frame and show what remains blocked or unknown per state.
Keep test/sample fixtures in explicit test lineage only and do not seed production tenants.
Use the shared 800×600 setup task frame for one-question organisation, scoped salesperson-line connection, authorised intake and explicit unavailable-analysis/manual-review states.

positive: A new tenant sees a truthful setup path in the shared 800×600 viewport-clamped task frame and can resume accepted intake work after reload.
A provisioned owner can resume the one-question setup with authorised intake while unavailable analysis remains manual review only.
negative: An empty tenant, upload preview, or unreviewed proposal cannot claim sellable products, stock, external connections, or activation.
A setup draft, phone chip, upload preview or manual review cannot claim provider connection, model analysis, stock, sellable catalogue or activation.

doneConditions: Provisioning, empty state, intake, resume, permission, and no-demo-data tests pass.
requiredEvidence: Activation state trace, intake recovery test, and production-fixture denial result.
1280×800, 390×844 and 320×740 setup frame/keyboard/reload/permission/intake evidence.

title: Guided operating readiness and supported activation
summary: Complete the tenant activation checklist across people, commercial/stock policy, roleplay, connection tests, legal/billing gates, training/support, and optional rails without treating a finished checklist as deployment authority.
steps: Derive checklist state from durable configuration, test receipt, policy, and owner acceptance facts.
Run controlled roleplay/source-to-document/output exercises with test lineage and named gaps.
Offer targeted support/education and retain incomplete/optional rail states explicitly rather than blocking unrelated ready work.
Carry current role, connection-test, controlled-roleplay and owner-acceptance gates through setup resume without treating a manual review as activation.

positive: An owner can see the exact remaining activation fact, its responsible role, and its evidence/recovery route.
A controlled roleplay and accepted gate checklist identify the remaining activation fact and responsible authority.
negative: A tour completion, model suggestion, configured card, or untested connection cannot activate a high-risk production capability.
A roleplay turn, configured line or completed browser checklist cannot contact a customer or activate production.

doneConditions: All activation states, roleplay, receipt, gap, support, and owner-acceptance tests pass.
requiredEvidence: Activation checklist report, controlled roleplay trace, and owner-acceptance audit.
Controlled roleplay, activation-gate, revoke/reload and owner-acceptance evidence at 1280×800, 390×844 and 320×740.

title: Migration verification, cutover rehearsal, and tenant support recovery
summary: Migrate retained source and business records through review/report/reconciliation, rehearse rollback/compensation, and provide scoped support diagnostics with no unauthorized repair.
steps: Validate imported IDs, rows, totals, units, prices, archive state, source retention, and tenant scope before activation.
Rehearse forward migration, rollback/compensation, support diagnostics, and recovery in isolated environments.
Issue a tenant-readable report that separates accepted, skipped, ambiguous, failed, and review-needed facts.

positive: A rehearsal reports exact parity and recovery evidence for the selected tenant/test lineage.
negative: A migration, support session, or accepted report cannot silently reshape historical documents, access unrelated tenants, or authorize production cutover.

doneConditions: Migration parity, rollback/compensation, support access expiry, and activation acceptance exercises pass.
requiredEvidence: Migration verification report, rehearsal result, and scoped-support audit.

title: Release evidence board and full-system acceptance ledger
summary: Collect required contract, integration, end-to-end, accessibility, failure, recovery, performance, security, and operational evidence by task/control/state, reporting only verified scope.
steps: Require source/release/drive/scope/result links for every actual evidence entry and retain failed/blocked results.
Calculate task/control/state coverage with no substitution of a kit path for runtime or production proof.
Block promotion when required evidence is missing, stale, contradictory, or outside the selected release revision.

positive: The ledger reports an exact release scope, each required proof, and any remaining blocked or failed condition.
negative: A screenshot, design demo, partial test, green aggregate, or unrelated release cannot tick an unproven production boundary.

doneConditions: Evidence schema, task/control rollup, stale-proof, failure retention, and release-block tests pass.
requiredEvidence: Release ledger export and an intentional missing-proof gate failure.

title: Staged rollout, monitoring, rollback, and incident communications
summary: Prepare versioned deployment artifacts, safe rollout cohorts, monitored canary/rollback criteria, compensating migration path, operator ownership, and incident communication without self-authorizing production. Every cohort records the release profile's designed, enabled and independently proven capabilities; the order-review launch profile permits only its explicit active surface and cannot silently activate commercial, inventory, customer-outbound, supplier-intake or ERP leaves.
steps: Define immutable release version, schema compatibility, cohort, explicit release-profile capability matrix (designed/enabled/proven), success/failure thresholds, owner, and abort criteria.
Exercise rollback or compensating event, service/projection recovery, and operator communication in an isolated controlled environment.
Separate deployed, designed, enabled, independently proven, monitored, rolled back, and incident states with durable evidence.

positive: A controlled rollout can halt and return to the documented safe state with evidence of the exact reason and each capability's enabled/proven boundary.
negative: A build, preview, partial deployment, toggle, configured integration, or successful canary cannot bypass capability/release gates or represent full production acceptance.

doneConditions: Rollout/abort/rollback, schema compatibility, capability-matrix, monitoring, and incident-drill tests are complete.
requiredEvidence: Isolated rollout rehearsal, rollback result, alert/incident drill record, and order-review capability-matrix/disabled-surface proof.

title: Production authorization and owner-go gate
summary: Require the recorded explicit owner authorization only after all evidence, operational ownership, recovery, security, accessibility, provider, billing, and tenant activation gates are satisfied.
steps: List every required gate, evidence revision, unresolved risk, owner, and rollout/rollback decision in one reviewable authorization record.
Require explicit recorded owner go after the evidence review; preserve denial/defer conditions as first-class outcomes.
Bind enablement to the approved release/cutover record and expire/revoke it if material evidence changes.

positive: A production enablement decision references the exact reviewed release and owner authorization.
negative: A task status, passing build, agent action, or implied permission cannot deploy, enable external sends, or override a production gate.

doneConditions: Authorization/deny/defer/expiry and evidence-change invalidation tests pass.
requiredEvidence: Owner-go record template, deliberate-denial test, and release binding audit.

title: Public documentation build and publication gate
summary: Generate the product documentation site solely from the public canonical allowlist and task graph, validate source hashes, links, task/control coverage, and keep internal historical material out of the published artifact.
steps: Allowlist selected public canonical Markdown and taskgraph records; reject private-note links, secrets, host addresses, and disallowed source paths.
Render a responsive hierarchy, sidebar, table of contents, search, task/control deep links, and source/revision manifest next to the app artifact.
Fail build for missing core docs, unsafe content, invalid dependencies, unmapped obligations/controls, broken public links, or unverifiable evidence status.

positive: The generated site exposes only approved documents and a traceable task/control graph with hashes.
negative: A legacy operating note, raw source/customer text, credential, address, or broken private link cannot enter the public build.

doneConditions: The documentation generator validates cleanly, rejects deliberate unsafe/missing/unmapped fixtures, and renders the expected local directory.
requiredEvidence: Build manifest, validation report, public-link check, and negative publication-gate test.
